deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.

display_name.description: Human-readable display name of this API key. Modifiable by user.
display_name.rationale: Human-readable name for the API key, used for identification only. It has no effect on access, restrictions, or exposure, so it is not a security policy target.

name.description: The resource name of the key. The name must be unique within the project, must conform with RFC-1034, is restricted to lower-cased letters, and has a maximum length of 63 characters. In another word, the name must match the regular expression: `[a-z]([a-z0-9-]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?`.
name.rationale: Resource identifier of the API key. Naming is a team choice with no security effect; we do not constrain resource names.

project.rationale: Project the API key belongs to. This is a project selector/identifier; enforcing a specific project would require knowing a team's project and is overreaching.

service_account_email.description: The email of the service account the key is bound to. If this field is specified, the key is a service account bound key and auth enabled. See [Documentation](https://cloud.google.com/docs/authentication/api-keys?#api-keys-bound-sa) for more details.

restrictions.android_key_restrictions.description: The Android apps that are allowed to use the key.

restrictions.android_key_restrictions.al.description: A list of Android applications that are allowed to make API calls with this key.
The package name of the application.
restrictions.android_key_restrictions.al.rationale: Restricting Android package names ensures that only trusted mobile applications can use the API key.

restrictions.android_key_restrictions.al.description: The SHA1 fingerprint of the application. For example, both sha1 formats are acceptable : DA:39:A3:EE:5E:6B:4B:0D:32:55:BF:EF:95:60:18:90:AF:D8:07:09 or DA39A3EE5E6B4B0D3255BFEF95601890AFD80709. Output format is the latter.
restrictions.android_key_restrictions.al.rationale: Restricting SHA1 fingerprints prevents unauthorised Android applications from using the API key.

restrictions.api_targets.description: A restriction for a specific service and optionally one or more specific methods. Requests are allowed if they match any of these restrictions. If no restrictions are specified, all targets are allowed.

restrictions.api_targets.methods.description: Optional. List of one or more methods that can be called. If empty, all methods for the service are allowed. A wildcard (*) can be used as the last symbol. Valid examples: `google.cloud.translate.v2.TranslateService.GetSupportedLanguage` `TranslateText` `Get*` `translate.googleapis.com.Get*`
restrictions.api_targets.methods.rationale: Limiting callable methods reduces the attack surface of the API key and prevents unintended API usage.

restrictions.api_targets.service.description: The service for this restriction. It should be the canonical service name, for example: `translate.googleapis.com`. You can use `gcloud services list` to get a list of services that are enabled in the project.
restrictions.api_targets.service.rationale: Restricting API targets ensures that the API key can only be used with approved Google Cloud services, reducing the risk of misuse.

restrictions.browser_key_restrictions.description: The HTTP referrers (websites) that are allowed to use the key.

restrictions.browser_key_restrictions.al.description: A list of regular expressions for the referrer URLs that are allowed to make API calls with this key.
restrictions.browser_key_restrictions.al.rationale: Restricting HTTP referrers prevents unauthorized websites from using the API key.

restrictions.ios_key_restrictions.description: The iOS apps that are allowed to use the key.

restrictions.ios_key_restrictions.allowe.description: A list of bundle IDs that are allowed when making API calls with this key.
restrictions.ios_key_restrictions.allowe.rationale: Restricting iOS bundle identifiers ensures that only trusted iOS applications can use the API key.

restrictions.server_key_restrictions.description: The IP addresses of callers that are allowed to use the key.

restrictions.server_key_restrictions.all.description: A list of the caller IP addresses that are allowed to make API calls with this key.
restrictions.server_key_restrictions.all.rationale: Restricting server IP addresses ensures that only trusted network locations can use the API key.
